newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook--Copper seen jumpy ahead of options.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook--Copper seen jumpy ahead of options.

text.p: Base metal market activity this week will be dominated by the run-up to Wednesday's July option declarations, particularly in copper, against a background of July tightness, traders said.
Copper prices finished last week at $2,418 a tonne, having been bounced around between $2,355 and $2,594 in the five previous trading days. The cash/threes backwardation was $151/155.
"We've got a declaration coming up, the July date is very tight, but you just cannot say which way it will go," one trader said.

The volatile futures market and the fluctuating backwardation meant that some unexpected strikes were now vulnerable on copper. Consequently, it was difficult to foresee which strike the July date would gravitate around.

Option traders have been trying to square up their positions, unwilling to take the chance of ending up short July after declaration. July/August was particularly tight, standing at $100 backwardation.
"The real fear is ending up short of July. Most people would like to be square of July, or failing that they would settle for being a little long," an options trader said.
Among the other metals, zinc was expected to maintain its current strong run, with prices ending last week near their highest for nearly seven years.
The market hit a high of $1,430 on Friday, and would now be targeting $1,450. However, some analysts were a little dubious about the advance on fundamental grounds.
There is a high level of exports from China this year, which would reduce the likely deficit between supply and demand, they said.

Meanwhile, nickel would be under pressure, having slumped to the lowest levels since January last Friday as the end of the current strike at Inco neared. Over the weekend, the union approved a labour settlement to end the four-week strike.
"I think most people expected Inco to settle -- it is getting near their maintenance shutdown, and they don't want it dragging on," one said.
The market fell below the $7,000 mark on Friday and tumbled further to a low of $6,760 on Monday morning.
Aluminium was expected to be fairly uneventful either side of the option declaration, with the market pinned between good technical support at $1,560 and overhead selling at $1,600.
